title: Adaptive Replay Scheduler and Backfill Gateway for Console Usage Pipelines
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement an adaptive, quota-aware replay scheduler and a lightweight backfill gateway to improve reliability and observability of console usage analytics reprocessing jobs. This ticket covers API surface, scheduler heuristics, rate limiting integration with quotas, retry semantics, and end-to-end instrumentation for audits and cost accounting.
background: Our console usage pipelines require periodic reprocessing to fix schema drift, late-arriving events, and missed webhooks. Existing reprocess tooling is manual, single-threaded, and lacks priority awareness; customer dashboards have been stale during major backfills. We need a more robust orchestration layer that can schedule replays across partitions, respect Dedicated capacity quotas, and provide real-time progress to Console UX.
proposed_solution: Build a service called 'backfill-gateway' that exposes job creation and status endpoints. Implement an 'adaptive-replay-scheduler' that: 1) ingests a backfill plan (time ranges + partitions), 2) computes priority and parallelism based on realtime quota signals from quota-service, 3) shards work using time-window hints, 4) issues replay tasks to existing reprocessor workers via the existing job queue, and 5) emits traceable events to obs (trace id) and the console progress API. Include configurable safety caps, circuit breakers for errors, and optional dry-run mode.
acceptance_criteria: API to create backfill job with validation has OpenAPI spec and unit tests
Scheduler respects per-customer quota signals and reduces concurrency under pressure
Backfill progress visible in Console with sub-minute updates for jobs >10m partitions
End-to-end test demonstrating backfill that repairs schema-mapped events without data loss
Retry semantics implemented: idempotent reprocess attempts, exponential backoff, dead-lettering for permanent failures
Cost tagging present on emitted events for billing reconciliation
tasks: Implement scheduler core with plugin hooks for quota signals (Marco)
Integrate with job-queue and ensure idempotency tokens (Eng-queue team)
Add telemetry: traces, metrics (jobs.started, jobs.succeeded, jobs.failed, per-customer tokens used)
Console UX endpoint and lightweight polling view (PM + frontend)
Write chaos test simulating quota starvation and verify graceful throttling
Write runbooks for emergency job cancellation and rollback
risks: Aggressive parallelism could exceed Dedicated GPU capacity and increase cost
Incorrect idempotency could cause duplicate analytics events and inflate metrics
Long-running backfills may conflict with live reprocessing windows and cause contention
Insufficient observability makes it hard to triage stuck shards
decisions: Use existing reprocessor workers and job-queue rather than building new worker fleet to reduce surface area
Expose a dry-run mode that calculates estimated token usage and duration before execution
Scheduler will use a conservative default concurrency and ramp-up using additive increase to avoid bursts
